extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark that includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials. The collection took three stages: selecting subjects, recruiting annotators, and collecting questions from textbooks and online resources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning were performed: (1) lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify and eliminate duplicate problems; (2) problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. Additionally, approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students specializing in the relevant majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, and to select questions without immediately available answers. Authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students specializing in the relevant majors across 30 subjects.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark has a live-updating leaderboard. Version change log is maintained in the supplementary material.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which is defined as AI reaching at least the 90th percentile of skilled adults, potentially leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large multimodal models (LMMs) on expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning tasks. The benchmark is used under zero-shot settings to assess model capabilities without fine-tuning.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.

inLanguage.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines

isLiveDataset.evidence: The live-updating leaderboard is available at: https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. This process results in a diverse collection of 13K questions from various sources.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. The annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: We recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The live-updating leaderboard is available at: https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Level 3, or Expert AGI, marks a critical milestone. It denotes an AI system that reaches 'at least 90th percentile of skilled adults' in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve 'the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor' for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting to assess the capability of models to generate accurate answers without fine-tuning or few-shot demonstrations on our benchmark. We believe MMMU will stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
